headline: High-risk shared-browser/web-app pairing: open-webui can ingest and act on PDF content from pdf.js, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, documents, browsers, and MCP/tool outputs, while pdf.js renders attacker-controlled PDFs in a browser context. The pair creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if PDF text is copied or forwarded into open-webui, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF PDF text from pdf.js is copied into open-webui prompts or notes
IF open-webui is configured to ingest document contents from a shared workspace
IF an MCP or browser bridge forwards PDF-derived text into open-webui without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic import of PDF text into chat context
Use a separate workspace for PDFs and chat artifacts
Add a provenance banner before any pasted PDF content
Restrict MCP/tool connectors to trusted sources only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches API keys, persistent memory, files, and cloud-connected APIs, while pdf.js handles PDF files locally. If both share a workspace or the PDF contains secrets, open-webui can leak those contents through its broader egress surfaces; pdf.js itself is local-only, so the risk is driven by open-webui's outbound paths.
conditions: IF PDFs containing secrets are opened in pdf.js and then imported into open-webui
IF open-webui is connected to any external API or search connector
IF both agents share a mounted volume or browser profile
mitigations: Keep PDFs and chat data in separate directories
Remove API keys from the open-webui runtime when not needed
Disable external connectors during document review
Use local-only inference for sensitive PDFs
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace access controls and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad filesystem and network-related capabilities, while pdf.js is browser-based and network-egress-free. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited; uncertainty remains because shared browser sessions or mounted files are possible but not documented as default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF open-webui is configured to modify files that pdf.js is simultaneously reading
IF the orchestrator shares a browser profile or session state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same PDF or artifact
Run pdf.js in a read-only browser context
Serialize access through a simple operator checklist
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate and route outputs through tools, and pdf.js can supply document text that may be treated as authoritative by the operator or downstream prompts. The pair supports a classic unverified-document pipeline, but there is no evidence that pdf.js itself takes actions, so I keep this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF text extracted from pdf.js is pasted into open-webui without verification
IF open-webui is instructed to summarize or act on PDF claims as facts
IF downstream tools in open-webui execute actions based on those claims
mitigations: Require a human verification step before acting on PDF-derived claims
Ask open-webui to cite page numbers and quote spans
Keep pdf.js output in read-only review mode
Mark unverified PDF text as draft only
requires-engineering: add source-grounding checks before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, persistent memory, and cloud-connected data classes, while pdf.js only processes PDF documents. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to general handling gaps rather than a documented breach path; pdf.js is not cited beyond its local PDF scope.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into open-webui's persistent memory or external connectors
IF PDFs contain data subject to retention or residency rules
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Do not store regulated PDFs in persistent memory
Disable analytics and external logging for sensitive sessions
Review retention settings before uploading documents
Use local-only processing for regulated files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per workspace
